items.title: Federal Housing Fund Backs $1 Million in Mississauga Rebates for Basement and Garage Conversions
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, homeowners can tap more than $1 million in funding through the city's Gentle Density Incentive Program to help cover the cost of adding new licensed units to their properties. The city says the incentives apply to units such as basement apartments, garage conversions, garden suites, triplexes and fourplexes, lowering costs for homeowners creating new housing. Mississauga reports it has issued more than $839,000 in gentle density incentives so far, funded through the federal Housing Accelerator Fund. In most cases, the city says homeowners building one or two units automatically get a rebate covering permit fees once construction is complete. The city notes homeowners building a fourplex may qualify for extra incentives, and it is promoting the program ahead of National Housing Day. The funding is available for a limited time, according to the city.

items.title: Brampton Assault Call Leads Police to Fatal Standoff at UTM Student Residence
items.summary: According to the SIU, Peel police received a 911 call Monday afternoon after a man allegedly assaulted a woman in Brampton, and officers located him later that evening at a student residence on the University of Toronto Mississauga campus near Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road. The watchdog says a gunshot was heard and the 19 year old man was found with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, and he was pronounced dead early Tuesday morning. Before the shooting was confirmed, UTM issued an alert telling students to shelter in place because of police activity near the McLuhan Court residence, according to the university. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has opened an investigation into the circumstances of the death, the SIU said. UTM said Tuesday it was saddened by the death and the investigation, and confirmed the campus would stay open while cancelling Tuesday classes.

items.title: Peel Police Charge Two Men, Including an Off-Duty Sudbury Officer, After Mississauga Hotel Dispute
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, two men were charged following an altercation at a Mississauga hotel on Nov. 7, including 40 year old Jeffrey Mussen, a sergeant with the Greater Sudbury Police Service's Intimate Partner Violence Unit who was off duty at the time. Peel police told CTV News that Mussen was charged with assault, while 48 year old Matthew Bedard was charged with uttering threats to cause death or bodily harm. Both men were released at the scene and will appear in court later, according to Peel police. Greater Sudbury Police Service spokesperson Kaitlyn Dunn told CTV News the service is aware of the charge against Mussen but said it would be inappropriate to comment since the matter is before the courts and occurred outside its jurisdiction. Sudbury police said allegations of criminal conduct involving its members go through the proper legal and internal processes.

items.title: Fergus Avenue Building Sees Extended Police Presence Over Person in Crisis
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, officers responded to a person in crisis at an apartment building on Fergus Avenue in Mississauga on Wednesday afternoon. Police say the incident is contained to a single unit and that there is no concern for the safety of other residents in the building. The force said in a social media update that there will be an extended police presence in the area as the situation continues. Peel police are asking drivers to avoid the area and seek alternate routes if possible. Residents who are unsure whether they can access the property are being told to speak with an officer on scene for direction, according to the police bulletin.

items.title: Mississauga to Host December Open House on $500M Plan for Third MiWay Bus Garage
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga will host a public open house on Dec. 8 to present plans for a new transit facility near Mississauga Road and Meadowvale Boulevard that would become MiWay's third bus garage. The outlet reports MiWay keeps its roughly 500 buses at two facilities, one in the Erindale area and one in Malton, both of which are at full capacity and cannot accommodate additional buses. City officials said the new site would need to hold between 170 and 280 buses, with an estimated capital cost of more than $500 million, according to insauga.com. Former mayor Carolyn Parrish wrote to the federal government earlier this year seeking funding, warning that without a new facility the city's shift to zero emission buses would be constrained, the outlet reported. Insauga.com notes the facility is meant to support the city's Climate Change Action Plan.

items.title: Body-Camera Footage Challenges Officer's Timeline in Peel Police Shooting Inquest Testimony
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a Peel police tactical officer faced questions at a coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique about how long it took to call for medical help after the fatal shooting. Const. Marc Charlebois testified he arrived at the Mississauga complex about 20 minutes after the shooting and broke a rear window, where he saw blood and heard Francique's laboured breathing, the outlet reports. After reviewing video Wednesday, Charlebois said he now believes he did not realize Francique was badly hurt until he broke a second window, basing that on his own body language in the footage, according to insauga.com. Lawyers pushed back, arguing Charlebois would have known from his breathing alone, the outlet reported. A lawyer for the Black Action Defence Committee said Charlebois had other information pointing to a medical emergency, according to insauga.com.

items.title: Mystery Mississauga Ticket Holder Has Yet to Claim $38-Million Lotto 6/49 Jackpot
items.summary: According to OLG, a Lotto 6/49 Gold Ball ticket sold in Mississauga has won a $38 million jackpot from Wednesday night's draw, one of Ontario's biggest lottery prizes this year. The lottery corporation confirmed Thursday that the winning ticket for the Nov. 11 draw was sold in the city, though the winner's identity has not yet been made public. OLG says the winner must come forward and have their ticket validated before officially claiming the prize. The outlet reports the winning Gold Ball number was 43779735-02, according to OLG's published results. Elsewhere in Ontario, OLG says a ticket holder in the Leeds and Grenville region separately won a $1 million Encore prize in the same draw. OLG notes the next Lotto 6/49 draw takes place Saturday, Nov. 14, offering another chance at a life changing jackpot.

items.title: Half-Acre Expansion and New Play Area Headline Final Bert Fleming Park Design Before Public Vote
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the City of Mississauga is asking west end residents for a final round of feedback before putting its revised redesign of Bert Fleming Park into motion. The outlet reports the updated plan includes changes to naturalization areas, park trails and open lawn space, along with an expanded children's play area and new gathering spaces with seating. City officials updated the blueprint after feedback from residents last spring and are now asking people to review the newest version and complete a survey by Dec. 14, according to insauga.com. The outlet notes the park, on The Credit Woodlands near Mississauga Road, is being enlarged by half an acre as part of the Credit Woodlands Integrated Road Project, which will also add pedestrian crossings and sidewalks. Insauga.com reports officials say the input will help shape a park that reflects the community's needs.

items.title: Hospice Mississauga Launches Ornament Campaign With $100,000 Matching Pledge From Longo Foundation
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Hospice Mississauga is launching its Trees of Remembrance campaign with a free community celebration Thursday at Sherwood Village Mall, inviting residents to honour loved ones while raising money for its programs. The outlet reports the Light Up the Holidays Social will feature decorated holiday trees, community activities and presentations, and residents can create a personalized remembrance ornament by submitting a message or memory through the Hospice Mississauga website. Volunteers will prepare the ornaments and hang them on the trees, according to insauga.com. The campaign continues Jan. 8 with trees sponsored and decorated by local businesses, community groups and individuals, the outlet reported. Insauga.com notes the fundraising goal is $300,000, with the Longo Family Foundation offering to match holiday contributions up to $100,000.

items.title: City Urges Residents to Bookmark Favourites Ahead of Winter Program Registration
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents are being urged to register early for winter recreation and culture programs and March Break camps before popular spots fill up. The city says in a notice to residents that winter is a good time to learn something new, stay active and connect with the community, and that programs are open to all ages, interests and abilities. Officials are encouraging residents to browse Active Mississauga now and build a wish list by bookmarking programs ahead of registration opening in November for residents and in December for non-residents. The city reports in-person registration is also available at community centres during service desk hours for those who prefer not to book online. According to the city, the wish list approach helps residents move quickly once registration opens, with options for ages from preschoolers to older adults.

items.title: Dundas Street Pizza Pizza Reopens Same Day After Peel Health Ordered It Shut
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, a Pizza Pizza location at 1093 Dundas St. W. in Mississauga was ordered closed during a Nov. 13 inspection but was allowed to reopen the same day. The health unit says inspectors routinely check local restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout food establishments to make sure they meet safety standards. Peel Public Health also issued conditional passes to several other food serving businesses and salons during recent rounds of inspections, according to the health unit. The outlet reports the closure order and conditional passes are part of the same routine inspection process that covers a wide range of Mississauga businesses. Peel Public Health notes these checks happen on an ongoing basis across the region, not only in response to complaints.
